turns.request: Show me how the total operational carbon was computed.
turns.reply: The graph behind that answer is two nodes. `elements` reads `nrc_analytics_elements.csv` from the `nrc` source, 218 rows. `answer` aggregates it with no grouping: `sum(OperationalCarbon_kgCO2e_per_year) as Total, count(*) as Elements`. The result is Total 37,196.2, Elements 218 — the number the paper's Q1 quotes. Open it in the editor to check the aggregate expression yourself; there is no filter step, every one of the 218 rows is summed.

turns.request: Which files would the reviewer need?
turns.reply: Six committed files cover the model and its analytics, plus the sample notebooks already in `samples/notebooks/`. The two IFC models: `duplex-base.ifc` (2,380,763 bytes), the model before enrichment, and `duplex-enriched.ifc` (2,707,239 bytes), the copy the property sets were written into. Three CSVs: `nrc_analytics_elements.csv` (35,069 bytes), the 218 element rows behind the total above; `nrc-metrics.csv` (2,554 bytes), the metric dictionary; and `door_verdicts.csv` (10,403 bytes), the DC-W1 evidence. And the three notebooks already saved: `nrc-eight-questions.notebook.json` (58,464 bytes), `nrc-test-kit.notebook.json` (66,355 bytes), and `nrc-door-check.notebook.json` (24,270 bytes) — this one joins them once it is saved.
